name: Architecture Duel
premise: Competing teams answer the same scenario by assembling a system from artifact cards.
setup: Deal seven artifacts to each player. Reveal a scenario, two constraints, and one failure condition.
turn: Play one artifact, name its real mechanism, and connect it to the shared graph. Unsupported buzzword play is invalid.
scoring: Gain structure points for typed connections, resilience points for credible counterforces, and lose points when another player exposes an unhandled shadow.
testedExample: A city needs a benefits system during disasters. Client–Server plus Identity and Access Management creates a center; Mesh Network and Disaster Recovery counter outage risk; Principal–Agent Problem exposes outsourced eligibility decisions. The distributed design wins only after naming reconciliation and appeal.

name: Venture Runway
premise: Build a venture without letting story, capital, or scale outrun evidence.
setup: Each player receives a Founder, three Option tokens, twelve Runway, and five random artifacts.
turn: Spend Runway to test, build, hire, or finance. Every growth move adds a Shadow card unless supported by evidence.
scoring: Survive six cycles with Product–Market Fit evidence, a credible institution, and at least three Runway. Highest valuation does not win.
testedExample: A logistics founder takes Venture Capital Fund and builds Data Center before a Usability Test. Premature Scaling triggers; a Pivot preserves the routing capability, but the player survives only by discarding the Founder Myth and funding a smaller verified market.

name: Protocol Council
premise: Independent factions must create a shared protocol without surrendering incompatible interests.
setup: Each player draws a stakeholder mandate, private risk, and veto. Reveal one shared resource.
turn: Propose clauses using Protocol and Force artifacts. Every clause must name state, authority, exception, and exit.
scoring: The protocol succeeds if it survives three adversarial events and no participant is forced below its legitimacy threshold.
testedExample: A shared AI evidence network uses Standard, Oracle Network, and Audit. A vendor proposes one central model; the council adds Fork and Multiple Sources. Consensus is slower but survives a poisoned-source event.

name: Institutional Memory
premise: Reconstruct why a failing institution works the way it does before changing it.
setup: Lay one Legacy, one Failure, and one Place face up. Shuffle remaining cards by era.
turn: Players add predecessors, promises, and consequences to a shared lineage. A redesign cannot erase a promise that has not been named.
scoring: Earn continuity for preserved obligations, release for retired assumptions, and repair for tested migration paths.
testedExample: A hospital scheduling system looks like Vendor Lock-In. The group traces it through Mainframe, Transaction Processing, and Internal Control; the redesign keeps auditability while replacing the interface in reversible stages.
